title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 9th District
area: Memphis and surrounding Shelby County, under the congressional map Tennessee redrew in May 2026.

context.text: Tennessee redrew its congressional district boundaries in May 2026 (mid-decade redistricting). Incumbent Rep. Steve Cohen (D), who has held this seat since 2007, withdrew from the Democratic primary and is not on the November 3 ballot.

State Rep. Justin Pearson won the Democratic primary with 65.8% of the vote, defeating state Sen. London Lamar and two others. State Sen. Brent Taylor won the Republican primary with 46.0% of the vote in a four-candidate field.
Tennessee state Sen. Brent Taylor announced his campaign for the seat in May 2026, before Rep. Cohen withdrew from the race.

candidates.name: Justin Pearson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Democratic primary with 65.8% of the vote

summary.text: Justin Pearson is a Memphis state representative first elected in a January 2023 special election, who gained national attention after being expelled from and then reinstated to the Tennessee House following gun-control protests on the House floor. He is a community organizer and nonprofit founder running as the Democratic nominee for the 9th District.

background.text: Graduated from Mitchell High School in Memphis.
Career experience as a community organizer; founded a nonprofit organization.

Appointed by the Shelby County Commission as acting state representative for District 86 on January 24, 2023, then won the March 14, 2023 special election to formally take the seat; re-elected in 2024.

priorities.text: Campaign platform calls for a federal jobs guarantee, a true living minimum wage, and passage of the PRO Act to protect workers' right to organize.
Says he supports passing Medicare for All and investing in rural hospitals and the VA healthcare system.
Campaign platform calls for gun-safety measures including permits to carry, a ban on assault rifles, and background checks with cooling-off periods.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for passing Medicare for All and investing in rural hospitals and VA healthcare.
Campaign platform calls for permits to carry, a ban on assault rifles, and background checks with cooling-off periods for firearm purchases.
Campaign platform calls for ensuring the minimum wage is a true living wage.
Campaign platform calls for making billionaires and big corporations pay their fair share.
Campaign platform calls for fully funding public education and reining in what he calls school voucher "scams."

record.text: As a Tennessee state representative, was expelled from the Tennessee House on April 6, 2023 by a 69-26 vote on House Resolution 63, after participating in a March 30, 2023 protest at the State Capitol in support of gun-control laws; was reinstated in an acting capacity by the Shelby County Commission on April 12, 2023, and won a special election on August 3, 2023 to formally return to the seat.

candidates.name: Brent Taylor
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Republican primary with 46.0% of the vote in a four-candidate field

summary.text: Brent Taylor is a Tennessee state senator and funeral director who previously served on the Memphis City Council. He is the Republican nominee for the 9th District, running on public safety and support for President Trump's agenda.

background.text: Earned a degree in mortuary science from Northwest Mississippi Community College; worked as a funeral director.
Served on the Memphis City Council from 1995 to 2007 and on the Shelby County Election Commission.
Elected to the Tennessee State Senate, District 31, in 2022.

priorities.text: Campaign centers on public safety, saying Memphis has been "terrorized by criminals" under what he calls a "soft-on-crime" district attorney.
priorities.quote: For far too long, Memphians have been forced to watch as a soft-on-crime Soros-backed District Attorney allowed our community to be terrorized by criminals. ... As your Congressman, I will continue to fight every single day to ensure the liberals' harmful, negligent policies never take root in Tennessee.

priorities.text: Says he will support President Trump's agenda in Washington, including cutting federal spending and regulations.
priorities.quote: In Washington, Brent will support President Trump's agenda: cutting reckless federal spending, slashing burdensome regulations, and delivering real economic relief to the hardworking people of our district.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he would fight to finish the border wall, deport people in the country illegally who have committed crimes, and end sanctuary policies.
positions.quote: finish the border wall, restore strong enforcement, deport criminal illegal immigrants, end sanctuary policies, and strengthen cooperation among federal, state, and local law enforcement so Tennessee families are protected.

positions.summary: Campaign centers on increased support for local law enforcement to address crime in Memphis.

record.text: Elected to the Tennessee State Senate, District 31, in 2022; previously served on the Memphis City Council from 1995 to 2007.
